learn.hook: A monk with a garden of pea plants cracked the code of inheritance long before anyone had seen a gene!
points: Gregor Johann Mendel studied garden pea plants, choosing clear contrasting traits: tall/short plants, round/wrinkled seeds, yellow/green seeds, violet/white flowers.
He crossed a pure tall plant (TT) with a pure short plant (tt). All first-generation (F1) plants were tall (Tt) — none were medium height.
The trait that appears in F1 is dominant (tall, T); the hidden one is recessive (short, t). A recessive trait shows only when both copies are recessive (tt).
When F1 plants were self-pollinated, the F2 generation had tall and short plants in the ratio 3 : 1. Genotypes were TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1.
Conclusion: each trait is controlled by a pair of factors (now called genes), one from each parent; the short trait was not lost in F1, only hidden.

example.q: Think it through: F1 tall plants (Tt) are self-pollinated and 400 F2 plants grow. About how many are short?
steps: Cross Tt × Tt: offspring are TT, Tt, Tt, tt.
Only tt is short: 1 out of 4.

learn.reallife: Farmers and scientists at Indian agricultural institutes use the same principles of inheritance to breed crops with useful traits like better yield.

games.title: Mendel check
items: In Mendel's cross of pure tall and pure short plants, F1 plants were all tall.
Tall is dominant, so every Tt plant is tall.
F1 plants of a TT × tt cross were of medium height.
There was no blending; all were tall.
A plant with genotype Tt is short.
One dominant T is enough to make it tall.
In F2, the genotype ratio TT : Tt : tt is 1 : 2 : 1.
Tt × Tt gives TT, Tt, Tt, tt.
A recessive trait can reappear in F2 even though it is hidden in F1.
Two Tt parents can each pass on t, giving tt.
Mendel worked with garden pea plants.
Peas have clear contrasting traits and are easy to cross.

quiz.q: In Mendel's cross TT × tt, what are the F1 plants?
quiz.explain: All F1 plants are Tt; tall is dominant, so all are tall.
steps: Parents: TT (pure tall) × tt (pure short).
Every F1 plant gets T from one parent and t from the other → Tt.
T (tall) is dominant over t, so every Tt plant is tall.
So all F1 plants are tall (none medium).
Answer: All tall
quiz.mistake: Expects blending of traits

quiz.q: What is the phenotypic ratio of tall to short plants in Mendel's F2 monohybrid cross?
quiz.explain: Tt × Tt gives 3 tall (TT, Tt, Tt) to 1 short (tt).
steps: F1 × F1: Tt × Tt.
Offspring: TT, Tt, Tt, tt.
Tall (TT, Tt, Tt) = 3; short (tt) = 1.
So the phenotypic ratio is 3 : 1.
Answer: 3 : 1
quiz.mistake: Confuses phenotype ratio with genotype ratio

quiz.q: In F2, about 400 plants were raised from F1 tall plants. How many would you expect to be short?
quiz.explain: One in four F2 plants is tt (short): 400 ÷ 4 = 100.
quiz.mistake: Uses the fraction of tall plants instead
steps: Short (tt) = 1/4 of F2
Answer: 100

quiz.q: Which trait is recessive in pea plants?
quiz.explain: Short height is recessive; it appears only in tt plants.
steps: A recessive trait appears only when both copies are recessive (tt).
In Mendel's peas, tall, round seeds and violet flowers are dominant.
Short stem is the recessive trait.
So the answer is short stem.
Answer: Short stem
quiz.mistake: Mixes up dominant and recessive traits

quiz.q: What is the genotype ratio TT : Tt : tt in the F2 generation?
quiz.explain: Tt × Tt gives one TT, two Tt and one tt.
steps: Tt × Tt gives: TT, Tt, tT, tt.
TT = 1, Tt = 2, tt = 1.
So the genotype ratio is 1 : 2 : 1.
Answer: 1 : 2 : 1
quiz.mistake: Uses the phenotypic ratio 3 : 1 for genotypes

quiz.q: A pea plant is tall. Its genotype could be —
quiz.explain: One dominant allele is enough for tallness, so a tall plant may be TT or Tt.
steps: Tall (T) is dominant; one T is enough to make a plant tall.
So a tall plant can be TT or Tt.
tt plants are short.
So its genotype could be either TT or Tt.
Answer: Either TT or Tt
quiz.mistake: Thinks a dominant trait must come from two dominant copies

quiz.q: Why did the short trait reappear in F2 although all F1 plants were tall?
options: F1 plants carried the hidden short factor (t), and two t's came together in some F2 plants
quiz.explain: The recessive factor was present but masked in F1; tt combinations appear in F2.
steps: F1 plants were Tt: they carried the short factor t, hidden by T.
When F1 plants were self-pollinated, some F2 plants got t from both parents (tt).
tt plants are short, so the short trait reappeared.
Answer: F1 plants carried the hidden short factor (t), and two t's came together in some F2 plants
quiz.mistake: Thinks the recessive trait was lost in F1

quiz.q: Mendel's 'factors' are today called —
quiz.explain: The units controlling traits are genes, which are sections of DNA on chromosomes.
steps: Mendel said each trait is controlled by a pair of 'factors'.
Today these units are called genes (sections of DNA on chromosomes).
So Mendel's factors are genes.
Answer: Genes
quiz.mistake: Confuses genes with whole chromosomes

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Pure tall and pure short peas made only tall babies. Where did the short trait go?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Tall is dominant and short is recessive — it hides in F1 and comes back in F2 as 3 : 1!
teach.nudge: Close! Was the short trait lost, or just hidden? What happens in F2?

revise.summary: Mendel crossed pea plants with contrasting traits. Crossing pure tall (TT) with pure short (tt) gave all tall F1 plants; self-pollinating F1 gave tall and short plants in a 3 : 1 ratio, showing traits are controlled by pairs of factors (genes).

Tell dominant from recessive traits and genotype from phenotype
Use the ratios to predict numbers of plants
remember: F1 of TT × tt: all Tt, all tall
F2 genotype ratio TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1
A recessive trait shows only in tt; Mendel's 'factors' are now called genes
traps: F1 plants are not medium height; tall is fully dominant
A tall plant may be TT or Tt, not only TT
The short trait was hidden in F1, not lost

learn.hook: Your dimples, curly hair or ear shape are written in a coded instruction book you got from both parents!
points: A gene is a section of DNA that carries the instructions for a protein. Proteins control traits — e.g. a gene for an enzyme that makes a growth hormone affects plant height.
Each body cell has two copies of every gene, one from each parent. Both parents contribute almost equal amounts of genetic material to the child.
Genes lie on chromosomes. Germ cells get only one chromosome from each pair, so when two germ cells fuse, the full number is restored.
Dihybrid cross: round yellow (RRYY) × wrinkled green (rryy) → F1 all round yellow. In F2: round yellow 9, round green 3, wrinkled yellow 3, wrinkled green 1 — a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio.
New combinations (round green, wrinkled yellow) show that traits are inherited independently. Sexual reproduction thus produces variations.

example.q: Think it through: in a dihybrid F2 of 160 pea plants, about how many would have wrinkled green seeds?
steps: The F2 ratio is 9 : 3 : 3 : 1, a total of 16 parts.
Wrinkled green is 1 part.

learn.reallife: Families often notice a grandparent's trait — like the same eye shape — skipping one generation and reappearing; recessive genes explain how that can happen.

quiz.q: What does a gene directly control?
options: The making of a specific protein
The amount of water in a cell
quiz.explain: A gene is a section of DNA that provides the information for making a protein, which then affects a trait.
steps: A gene is a section of DNA.
It carries the instructions for making a specific protein.
That protein then affects a trait.
So a gene directly controls the making of a specific protein.
Answer: The making of a specific protein
quiz.mistake: Thinks genes act without proteins

quiz.q: In Mendel's dihybrid cross, what was the F1 generation?
quiz.explain: Round and yellow are dominant, so all RrYy F1 plants show round yellow seeds.
steps: Parents: round yellow (RRYY) × wrinkled green (rryy).
All F1 plants are RrYy.
Round (R) and yellow (Y) are dominant.
So all F1 plants are round yellow.
Answer: All round yellow
quiz.mistake: Expects the F2 ratio in F1

quiz.q: In a dihybrid F2 generation of 160 plants, how many are expected to have round yellow seeds?
quiz.explain: Round yellow is 9 out of 16 parts: 160 × 9/16 = 90.
quiz.mistake: Uses the fraction for a different phenotype
steps: Total parts = 9 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 16
Round yellow = 9 parts
Answer: 90

items: Round yellow
Round green
Wrinkled yellow
Wrinkled green

quiz.q: The appearance of new combinations like round green seeds in F2 shows that —
options: Traits are inherited independently of each other
Only the mother passes on traits
quiz.explain: Seed shape and seed colour were sorted separately, giving new combinations.
steps: The parents were round yellow and wrinkled green.
F2 had new combinations: round green and wrinkled yellow.
Shape and colour must have been sorted separately.
So traits are inherited independently of each other.
Answer: Traits are inherited independently of each other
quiz.mistake: Thinks traits from one parent always stay together

quiz.q: How many copies of each gene does a normal body cell have?
quiz.explain: One copy comes from each parent, so a body cell has two.
steps: Each body cell gets one copy of every gene from each parent.
1 (from mother) + 1 (from father) = 2.
So a body cell has 2 copies of each gene.
Answer: 2
quiz.mistake: Confuses body cells with germ cells

quiz.q: Why do germ cells contain only one set of chromosomes?
options: So the offspring has the right number after two germ cells fuse
Because they are made in leaves
quiz.explain: Two half-sets combine at fertilisation to restore the full number of chromosomes.
steps: At fertilisation two germ cells fuse.
Each germ cell carries one chromosome from each pair (one set).
Two sets together restore the full number in the offspring.
So germ cells have one set so the offspring has the right number.
Answer: So the offspring has the right number after two germ cells fuse
quiz.mistake: Thinks chromosome number doubles every generation

quiz.q: A tall plant has more of a certain plant hormone. How is this linked to its gene?
options: The gene makes an efficient enzyme, which produces more hormone and makes the plant taller
The gene is the hormone itself
Genes have nothing to do with height
quiz.explain: Genes code for proteins such as enzymes; an efficient enzyme makes more hormone, affecting height.
steps: Genes carry instructions for proteins, such as enzymes.
An efficient enzyme makes more of the growth hormone.
More hormone makes the plant taller.
So the gene makes an efficient enzyme, which produces more hormone and a taller plant.
Answer: The gene makes an efficient enzyme, which produces more hormone and makes the plant taller
quiz.mistake: Thinks genes act directly as hormones

quiz.q: Which statement about inheritance in humans is correct?
options: Both parents contribute practically equal amounts of genetic material
Genes are passed only to sons
quiz.explain: Each parent contributes one copy of every gene, i.e. almost equal genetic material.
steps: Each parent passes on one copy of every gene.
So the child gets practically equal genetic material from the mother and the father.
So both parents contribute practically equal amounts of genetic material.
Answer: Both parents contribute practically equal amounts of genetic material
quiz.mistake: Thinks one parent contributes more

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'I got my mother's beak and my father's feathers! How are traits passed on?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Genes on chromosomes come from both parents, and they make the proteins that build my traits!
teach.nudge: Good! Who gives you your genes, and where are they found?

revise.summary: Genes are sections of DNA that make proteins, and proteins control traits. Each cell has two copies of every gene, one from each parent. Mendel's dihybrid cross gave a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio, showing traits are inherited independently.

Explain why germ cells carry only one set of chromosomes
Work out the F1 and F2 of a dihybrid cross

Each body cell has 2 copies of every gene; both parents contribute almost equally
Dihybrid F1 (RRYY × rryy): all round yellow
F2: round yellow 9 : round green 3 : wrinkled yellow 3 : wrinkled green 1
traps: Don't use 3 : 1 for a dihybrid cross; it is 9 : 3 : 3 : 1
New combinations (round green, wrinkled yellow) show independent inheritance, not mistakes
Germ cells have one set of chromosomes, not two

learn.hook: Whether a baby is a girl or a boy is decided at the very moment of fertilisation — by a tiny chromosome!
points: Different species decide sex in different ways. In some reptiles, the temperature at which fertilised eggs are kept decides the sex; some snails can change sex.
Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes: 22 pairs are autosomes, and 1 pair is the sex chromosomes.
Females have a perfect pair of X chromosomes (XX). Males have one X and one shorter Y chromosome (XY).
Every egg from the mother carries an X. Half the sperm carry X and half carry Y.

If an X-sperm fertilises the egg, the child is a girl (XX); if a Y-sperm does, the child is a boy (XY). So the sex of the child is decided by which chromosome comes from the father, and the chance of each is 50%.

example.q: Think it through: a family has three daughters. A relative says the mother is 'responsible'. What does science say?
steps: The mother's eggs always carry an X chromosome.
Whether the child is a girl or a boy depends on whether the sperm carries X or Y.
Each birth is a separate 50 : 50 chance, so no one is to blame.
example.answer: Science shows the mother is not responsible: the child's sex depends on the chromosome in the sperm, and it is a matter of chance.

learn.reallife: Knowing that sex is decided by chance and chromosomes helps us respect girls and boys equally — every child is welcome.

quiz.q: How many pairs of chromosomes are there in a human body cell?
quiz.explain: There are 23 pairs (46 chromosomes): 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes.
steps: Humans have 22 pairs of autosomes.
They also have 1 pair of sex chromosomes.
22 + 1 = 23 pairs (46 chromosomes in all).
So there are 23 pairs.
Answer: 23
quiz.mistake: Confuses pairs with the total number

quiz.q: What are the sex chromosomes of a human male?
quiz.explain: Males have one X and one Y chromosome.
steps: Females have a pair of X chromosomes (XX).
Males have one X and one shorter Y chromosome.
So a human male has XY.
Answer: XY
quiz.mistake: Swaps male and female sex chromosomes

quiz.q: Which parent's chromosome decides the sex of a child?
options: Mother's, because eggs carry X or Y
Father's, because sperm carry either X or Y
Both equally decide it by choice
quiz.explain: All eggs carry X; it is the sperm (X or Y) that decides the child's sex.
steps: Every egg from the mother carries an X chromosome.
Half the sperm carry X and half carry Y.
So the sperm decides the sex of the child.
So it is the father's chromosome, because sperm carry either X or Y.
Answer: Father's, because sperm carry either X or Y
quiz.mistake: Believes the mother decides the baby's sex

quiz.q: What is the probability that a child will be a girl?
quiz.explain: Half the sperm carry X and half carry Y, so the chance is 1/2 each time.
steps: Every egg carries X.
Half the sperm carry X (girl) and half carry Y (boy).
Chance of an X-sperm = 1/2.
So the probability of a girl is 1/2.
Answer: 1/2
quiz.mistake: Thinks earlier births change the chance

quiz.q: In some reptiles, the sex of the young is decided by —
options: The temperature at which the fertilised eggs are kept
quiz.explain: In some reptiles, incubation temperature determines the sex of the offspring.
steps: In some reptiles, sex is not decided by chromosomes.
The temperature at which fertilised eggs are kept decides it.
So the answer is the temperature at which the fertilised eggs are kept.
Answer: The temperature at which the fertilised eggs are kept
quiz.mistake: Assumes all animals use the XX/XY system

quiz.q: A sperm carrying a Y chromosome fertilises an egg. The baby will be —
options: A girl, if the mother eats well
quiz.explain: The egg gives X and the sperm gives Y, making XY — a boy.
steps: The egg always gives X.
The Y-sperm gives Y.
X + Y = XY, which is a boy.
So the baby will be a boy.
Answer: A boy
quiz.mistake: Forgets the egg always gives X

quiz.q: How many autosome pairs does a human have?
quiz.explain: Out of 23 pairs, 22 pairs are autosomes and 1 pair are sex chromosomes.
steps: Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes.
1 pair is the sex chromosomes.
23 − 1 = 22 pairs of autosomes.
Answer: 22
quiz.mistake: Counts the sex chromosome pair as an autosome

quiz.q: Which statement is correct?
options: All sperm carry the X chromosome
All eggs carry the X chromosome
The Y chromosome is longer than the X
quiz.explain: Eggs always carry X. The Y chromosome is shorter than X, and females are XX.
steps: All eggs carry X; half the sperm carry X and half carry Y.
The Y chromosome is shorter than X.
Females are XX, not XY.
So the correct statement is: all eggs carry the X chromosome.
Answer: All eggs carry the X chromosome
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which gamete varies

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Who decides whether a baby is a boy or a girl? My aunt says it's the mother!'
teach.praise: Tweet! The egg always gives X; the father's sperm gives X or Y — it's a 50 : 50 chance, not anyone's fault!
teach.nudge: Almost! Which parent's cell can carry either X or Y?

revise.summary: Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes, including one pair of sex chromosomes: females XX, males XY. All eggs carry X; sperm carry X or Y, so the father's sperm decides the child's sex, with a 50% chance each way.

Show with a cross why the sperm decides the child's sex

Female XX, male XY; the Y chromosome is shorter
X-sperm + egg → girl (XX); Y-sperm + egg → boy (XY); chance 1/2 each
In some reptiles, egg temperature decides sex
